module-structure.template:
""" Activity Tracking Module
Tracks user activity timestamps for silence detection and gate checks.
Redis Key Patterns: - user:{user_id}:last_activity -> ISO timestamp (TTL: 7 days) """
from datetime import datetime, timezone from typing import Optional import redis.asyncio as redis from redis import exceptions as redis_exceptions
from api.config import get_config from api.logging import get_logger
logger = get_logger(__name__)
# TTL for activity tracking: 7 days in seconds ACTIVITY_TTL = 604800
async def update_activity(user_id: str, redis_client: redis.Redis) -> None: """ Update user activity timestamp.
Stores ISO timestamp in Redis with 7-day TTL. Non-blocking, fire-and-forget operation.
Args: user_id: User identifier redis_client: Redis client from StateManager
Example: async with StateManager() as state: await update_activity("123456", state.redis_client) """ # Implementation here
async def get_last_activity(user_id: str, redis_client: redis.Redis) -> Optional[datetime]: """ Get last activity timestamp for user.
Returns datetime object or None if no activity found. Handles missing keys gracefully (returns None for new users).
Args: user_id: User identifier redis_client: Redis client from StateManager
Returns: datetime object with UTC timezone, or None if not found
Example: async with StateManager() as state: last_active = await get_last_activity("123456", state.redis_client) if last_active: print(f"Last active: {last_active.isoformat()}") """ # Implementation here

pattern.name: Test Activity Update
pattern.description: Test successful activity update with correct TTL
pattern.code:
@pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_update_activity_success(redis_mock): """Test successful activity update.""" user_id = "test_user_123"
await update_activity(user_id, redis_mock)
# Verify Redis setex was called redis_mock.setex.assert_called_once() call_args = redis_mock.setex.call_args[0]
# Check key format assert call_args[0] == f"user:{user_id}:last_activity"
# Check TTL (7 days = 604800 seconds) assert call_args[1] == 604800
# Check timestamp format (ISO with Z suffix) timestamp = call_args[2] assert timestamp.endswith("Z") assert "T" in timestamp

pattern.code:

redis_mock.get.return_value = stored_timestamp
result = await get_last_activity(user_id, redis_mock)
# Verify result is datetime object assert isinstance(result, datetime)

dev-notes.note: Keep activity tracking simple and fast. Single Redis write operation. Should complete in under 5ms under normal conditions.
Use fire-and-forget pattern. Activity tracking must never break chat flow. All exceptions caught and logged at WARNING level.
Reuse redis_client from StateManager context to avoid creating new connections. Pass state.redis_client as parameter to update_activity().
Timestamp format must match existing patterns (ISO with Z suffix). Use datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
7-day TTL chosen to balance: - Long enough for silence detection (days of inactivity) - Short enough to not store stale data indefinitely - Consistent with session/conversation TTLs in StateManager
